VIDEO TILE, FILES AND ARITHMETIC: AN INDEPENDENT REVIEW (Lantern 1.24.43, branch lantern-1.24.43)
=========================================================================================================

Written by a reviewer who did not write the tile, from its module headers and its code, with inputs of its own.
Nothing under src/, site/ or tests/ (outside this folder) was changed. Nothing was committed.

How to run:   python3 tests/fixtures/video_review1_1243/run.py            (about 3 minutes)
              python3 tests/fixtures/video_review1_1243/run.py edits mix   (only some sections)
Sections:     readers writers time edits keys mix loud color afx xchg scenes media
Needs:        node, ffmpeg/ffprobe (run here with 6.1.1), python3 with numpy, scipy, PIL. It makes all its media
              afresh in a temporary folder with ffmpeg; every random choice has a fixed seed. Math.random inside
              the tile is replaced by a seeded generator, so ids and the Dissolve blend repeat.
Result here:  1068 checks, 68 failed. Two full runs gave the same descriptions and the same verdicts.
              Check descriptions name only the case and the reference, never a value Lantern produced, so a run
              after a fix can be compared line by line with this one.

The references used (never Lantern's own idea of itself):
- ffprobe -show_packets/-show_streams for every reader; ffmpeg decoding (framemd5, md5, raw PCM) for every writer,
  and ffmpeg's own "-c copy" rewrite into the same container where two containers keep time differently;
- ffmpeg's ebur128 (integrated, momentary, short-term, true peak), EBU Tech 3341 cases 1-5, and BS.1770-4 worked
  in NumPy with the Recommendation's published 48 kHz filter coefficients;
- ffmpeg's lut3d and lut1d; the Cube LUT Specification's trilinear lookup worked in NumPy (for domains ffmpeg
  treats differently);
- SciPy (gaussian_filter, uniform_filter, median_filter, sobel, correlate, lfilter, freqz); the RBJ Audio EQ
  Cookbook worked in Python from its text; the W3C Compositing and Blending formula with the Photoshop blend
  functions; a direct linear solve for homographies; ffmpeg's default resampler for comparison;
- SMPTE 12M drop-frame arithmetic written independently in Python;
- what Premiere does for the edits (stated case by case below), and the CMX 3600 / FCP7 XML / WebVTT
  conventions as other programs write them.


THE MOST SERIOUS PROBLEMS (in order)
------------------------------------
1. MOV files with little-endian 24-bit, 32-bit or float PCM sound play as full-scale noise.
   ffmpeg (and programs built on it) store pcm_s24le / pcm_s32le / pcm_f32le in MOV as 'in24' / 'in32' / 'fl32'
   with an 'enda' atom (value 1 = little-endian) inside 'wave'. VIDEO_MP4_READ entry() never reads 'enda', so
   VIDEO_MEDIA pcmOf() reads them big-endian. Measured against ffmpeg's decode of the same file: s24le max
   error 1.35 (full scale is 1), s32le 1.35, f32le values up to 3.4e38 (and NaN). Big-endian in24 and 16-bit
   sowt/twos are right. This would come out of the speakers as loud noise, in preview and in export.
   (F64-F66: "sound of dec_s24le.mov / dec_s32le.mov / dec_f32le.mov decoded by Lantern")

2. Matroska/WebM files with PCM sound have no sound at all: VIDEO_MKV_READ marks A_PCM/INT/LIT tracks pcm=true,
   so VIDEO_MEDIA decodeAudio() sends them to viaPcm(), which reads t.chunks - a field only the MP4 and AVI
   readers make. It throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')". (F67-F68)

3. A 5.1 clip loses its centre channel (the dialogue of nearly every film and many cameras' surround tracks):
   VIDEO_MIX clipSound() takes channels 0 and 1 only (Math.min(2, a.data.length)), no fold-down. A 5.1 file
   with a tone only in the centre mixed to silence (-300 dB); ITU-R BS.775 fold-down would give -3 dB in each
   ear. The browser's decodeAudioData and WebCodecs both hand over all six channels, so this is reached.
   (F46)

4. Timeline edits that leave clips overlapping, re-ordered, or deleted that the person did not choose
   (VIDEO_EDIT, and the Q/W command in VIDEO_CMDS). Details under EDITS below. The ordinary ones:
   - Ripple Trim Next/Previous Edit to Playhead (W / Q) with V1 and A1 targeted (the default) on a linked clip
     moves everything after it TWICE: each per-track ripple trim already moves every sync-locked track.
     Clips overlap by 40 frames on V1 and A1. (F29-F30)
   - After Insert, Overwrite, Lift or Extract cuts a linked clip in two (VIDEO_EDIT split()), both halves keep
     the same link id, so the left picture's "partners" are its own sound AND both right halves. Selecting the
     left half and pressing Shift+Delete deletes the right half too. (F31-F32; razor() gives the right
     halves a new link, split() does not.)
   - Ripple Delete of two clips that are not side by side closes one gap of the combined span: A B C D minus
     A and C gives D at 0 and B at 30 (order swapped), overlaps in other layouts. (F15, F23; F14 is the same,
     reached through the shared link above)
   - A ripple trim when another sync-locked track has a clip across the cut point overlaps clips on that
     track (head and tail), and Speed/Duration with Ripple does the same. (F17-F19, F21, F24, F25)
   - Slide next to a gap moves the clip onto the clip beyond the gap. (F20, F26, F27)
   - A plain head trim outward on a clip with nothing before it goes past frame 0 (start -20). (F16, F33)

5. EDLs at 23.976, 29.97 non-drop and 59.94 non-drop are an hour-mark wrong both ways (VIDEO_XCHG):
   hour = Math.round(3600 * fps) frames is 86314 at 23.976, but 01:00:00:00 non-drop is frame 86400 (24 x 3600).
   Lantern writes record times from 00:59:56:10 (23.976), 00:59:56:12 (29.97 NDF), 00:59:56:24 (59.94 NDF);
   and reading a standard 23.976 EDL (record from 01:00:00:00, as Premiere and Resolve write it) puts every
   clip 86 frames (3.6 s) late. Drop-frame 29.97 and integer rates are right. 23.976 is the most common film
   rate. (F50-F53)

6. A .cube LUT with Resolve's LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE (or LUT_1D_INPUT_RANGE) line is silently garbled:
   parseCube() skips keywords matching /^[A-Z_]+$/, which has no digits, so "LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE 0.0 1.0" is
   taken as a row of the table (NaN 0 1) and every entry after it shifts by one channel. The picture comes out
   wrong by up to 242 levels with no error. (F47-F48)

7. The Video Limiter effect does not exist: VIDEO_FX_IMAGE adds it as type "limiter", and VIDEO_AFX later adds
   the Hard Limiter sound effect under the same type, replacing it. make('limiter') gives the sound effect; a
   saved project with a Video Limiter on a clip would run the audio limiter on a picture (TypeError).
   (F49)

8. Final Cut Pro XML (VIDEO_XCHG):
   - a file name with "&" (Q&A.mp4, Tom & Jerry.mov) makes Lantern's XML ill-formed: <pathurl> uses encodeURI,
     which leaves & as it is; Python's parser and Lantern's own reader refuse it. (F59-F60)
   - no <link> elements are written, though the header says the links between picture and sound are.
     (F58)
   - Premiere's XML gives -1 as <end>/<start> of the clips joined by a transition; readFcpxml() drops any clip
     with start < 0, so two clips with a Cross Dissolve between them both vanish on import. (F57)
   - speed written as Time Remap is not read back. (F61)

9. Keyframes change when a clip is cut or its head trimmed (VIDEO_EDIT shiftKeys): the keys it inserts at the
   cut are "linear", so Ease and Auto Bezier curves change shape (12 and 5.7 units on a 0-100 property); and when
   no keyframe lies inside the right part (its last keyframe is past the trimmed end) the right half becomes
   constant: a fade-out disappears (36.7 units). Linear keys come through exactly. (F34-F37)

10. AVI with WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE PCM (24-bit, more than 2 channels, or above 48 kHz - ffmpeg writes these so)
    is not taken as PCM ("audio tag 65534"), so it has no sound (no browser decodes AVI). (F1-F2)


EVERY FAIL, WITH ITS INPUT, WHAT LANTERN DID AND WHAT THE REFERENCE DID
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

READERS, WAV included (532 checks, 2 failed)
F1  mjpeg_pcm24.avi: ffmpeg -f lavfi testsrc2 320x240 25 fps + sine 48 kHz stereo, -c:v mjpeg -c:a pcm_s24le.
    ffprobe: pcm_s24le. Lantern: codec "audio tag 65534", pcm false. ffmpeg's WAV/AVI muxer writes
    WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE for >16 bits, >2 channels or >48 kHz; readAvi's strf parser keeps the tag 0xFFFE and
    never reads the SubFormat GUID (readWav does: it is right for the same cases).
F2  mjpeg_pcm96k.avi: the same with 96 kHz 16-bit: same result.

WRITERS (191 checks, 9 failed)
F3-F5  Remuxing an MP4 with AAC (sd_23976_mono441.mp4, ntsc5994.mp4, two_audio.mp4) through V.mp4.read ->
    V.mp4w.write: the file lasts 2.043 s where the original and ffmpeg's own "-c copy" rewrite last 2.000 s
    (1.536 vs 1.500).
    Cause: the reader keeps no sample durations; the writer gives the last AAC packet the previous packet's 1024
    and writes an edit list whose duration covers it, so the encoder's end padding (here 888 samples) is no
    longer cut. Pictures and sound otherwise decode sample-exact. Low severity (up to 21 ms of padding at 48 kHz);
    the same thing happens in export whenever the last AAC packet is partly padding.
F6  A 60 s VP8+Opus WebM rewritten by V.webmw.write: "ffmpeg -ss 55" reads 4,423,680 of 4,471,485 bytes
    (99%); on ffmpeg's own file it reads 131,647. Lantern writes Cues at the end but no SeekHead, so a reader
    cannot find them without walking every cluster. A long export will seek slowly in every player that reads
    WebM this way (ffmpeg, and Chrome, which uses ffmpeg's demuxer; not tried in a browser here).
F7-F8  WAV written with 6 channels (16- and 24-bit) uses format tag 1 (plain PCM), with no channel mask.
    Microsoft asks for WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE above 2 channels so a reader knows which speaker each channel is.
    ffmpeg reads the file and the values are right. Low severity (export writes stereo).
F9 WAV, 24-bit mono, 4801 frames: data chunk of 14,403 bytes has no pad byte; RIFF size 14,439 for a file of
    14,447 bytes. RIFF requires odd chunks to be padded. ffmpeg reads it anyway. Low severity.
F10 GIF: a 256x32 ramp of 64 greys (steps of 4), added with dithering off: comes back as 32 greys, error 4.
    nearestFn() caches the nearest palette entry per 15-bit colour (r>>3, g>>3, b>>3), so two colours closer than
    8 levels share one entry. A frame with 256 colours or fewer could be exact. Low severity: export dithers.
F11 GIF: 200x150 noise with exactly 256 colours, undithered: errors up to 26 levels. Median cut splits boxes by
    pixel count, so duplicate entries appear and some colours merge, besides the cache above. Low severity.

TIMECODE (24 checks, 2 failed)
F12 parseTc("00:00:10.5", 30 fps): the module's own comment gives this as 10.5 seconds; Lantern returns 305
    (10 s + 5 frames), not 315.
F13 parseTc("+2:00", 30 fps): the comment gives this as two seconds; Lantern returns null.
    Both are only the header's examples being wrong or unbuilt; low severity.

EDITS (98 checks, 20 failed)
The fuzz: 120 projects, each a random rate of 23.976/25/29.97/30/60, five media of 2.2 to 10 s, three V and
three A tracks, linked picture+sound pairs always on V(i)+A(i), then 40 random edits each, applied the way the
Timeline applies them to linked clips (VIDEO_TIMELINE apply(): partner trims with "keep"/"plain", slips on
partners, Ripple Delete with partners as C.selIds adds them). After every edit: no overlaps, whole frames >= 0,
no source outside [0, media length], every linked picture beside its sound, refused trims change nothing. Each
edit starts from a sound state: an edit that breaks something is counted against itself and undone.
F14 Ripple Delete of one clip and its linked sound: 3 of 262 left an overlap. These come through the shared
    link of F31 (the partners include the clip's other half elsewhere, so the selection is not one span).
F15 Ripple Delete of two random clips with their sound: 11 of 240 overlaps. See F23.
F16 A plain head trim outward: 38 cases of a clip starting before frame 0 (e.g. d=-50 -> start -50). See F33.
F17 A ripple head trim: 34 of 278 overlaps (see F24-F25); F18: one clip moved to start -5 (a ripple head trim of
    30 pulls a later clip on another track before 0).
F19 A ripple tail trim: 6 of 268 overlaps (see F24).
F20 Slide: 18 of 208 overlaps (see F26-F27).
F21 Speed/Duration with Ripple: 4 of 233 overlaps (the same as F24: later clips moved while a clip on another
    sync-locked track spans the old end).
F22 Speed/Duration: 5 of 233 clips show source past the media's end, e.g. 150% at 30 fps, srcIn 3.937 s +
    3.85 s > 7.77 s: the new length is rounded to whole frames with Math.round, so up to half a frame past
    the end. Trivial (the last frame's own start is inside the media); see F28.
F23 V1: A[0,30) B[30,60) C[60,90) D[90,120); rippleDelete([A, C]). Premiere: B at 0, D at 30. Lantern: D at 0,
    B at 30. rippleDelete() takes one span from the first start to the last end and moves only what starts after
    it; B (inside the span, kept) stays while D jumps over it.
F24 V1: X[0,60) Y[60,120); A2 (sync-locked): Z[0,100) W[100,150). trimTail(X, -20, "ripple"). Lantern moves W to
    80 while Z still ends at 100: overlap on A2. Premiere never lets a ripple overlap clips on a sync-locked
    track (it limits the trim or takes the frames from that track too).
F25 The same layout, trimHead(Y, +20, "ripple"): the same overlap.
F26 V1: X[0,30), gap, C[50,80) N[80,110). slide(C, -30): Lantern returns -30, C at [20,50) on top of X.
    slide() only looks at a neighbour exactly touching; a gap is not treated as a limit (Premiere treats a gap
    like a clip that can shrink to nothing).
F27 V1: X[0,30) C[30,60), gap, Y[70,100). slide(C, +20): C at [50,80) over Y.
F28 A 30-frame clip showing all of a 1.000 s file, Speed 70% with Ripple: 43 frames, srcIn+span = 1.00333 s.
    Trivial (rounding: Math.round(1/0.7*30) = 43 frames, 43/30*0.7 = 1.0033).
F29 The W command (VIDEO_CMDS C.trimTo, copied here line for line): linked v0/a0 [0,100), v1/a1 [100,200),
    v2/a2 [200,300) on V1/A1, both targeted (the default), playhead 60. Expected v0,a0 [0,60), v1 at 60, v2 at
    160. Lantern: v2 at 120, overlapping v1 [60,160) on both tracks. The V1 ripple trim moved everything on
    every sync-locked track; the A1 trim then moved it all again.
F30 The Q command at 140: v1 trimmed to [100,160), v2 should be at 160; Lantern puts it at 120 (overlap).
F31 Linked v/a [0,90) on V1/A1; insert a 20-frame clip on V2 at 45. Partners of the left picture: Lantern
    [V1 65+45, A1 0+45, A1 65+45]; expected only A1 0+45.
F32 ... then rippleDelete(left picture + its partners, as Shift+Delete does): Lantern deletes both halves
    (V1 and A1 end up empty); expected the right halves kept and moved to 20.
F33 A clip at frame 10 with 5 s of handle before its in point; trimHead(-30, "plain") with nothing before it:
    Lantern returns -30 and starts the clip at -20. Expected to stop at frame 0 (-10).

KEYFRAMES (13 checks, 4 failed)
F34 Opacity keys {0: 0 ease} {89: 100} on a 90-frame clip, Add Edit at 30: the right half's values differ from
    the original by up to 12.1 (at frame 67). The new key at the cut is "linear" and the eased curve is
    re-spread over the shorter span. Premiere keeps the curve.
F35 Auto Bezier keys {0:0} {30:80} {89:10}, cut at 50: up to 5.7 different (frame 20: the left part's curve
    changes because its end key is now a new linear one).
F36 Opacity {0: 100 linear} {120: 0} on a clip trimmed to 90 frames, cut at 45: the right half is held at 62.5
    instead of fading 62.5 -> 25.8 (difference 36.7 at its last frame). shiftKeys() adds an end key only when
    some key lies inside the part.
F37 Keys {0: 0 ease} {60: 100}, head trimmed by 20: the frames that stay differ by up to 12.2.

MIXER (37 checks, 9 failed)
F38-F42 Pure tones resampled to the 48 kHz sequence by VIDEO_MIX at(): distortion plus noise (THD+N, the
    residual after removing the best-fitting sine at the right pitch) is -64.7 dB (1 kHz from 44.1 kHz),
    -65.3 (5 kHz from 44.1), -56.3 (10 kHz from 44.1), -63.2 (1 kHz from 32 kHz), -66.0 (1 kHz from 22.05 kHz).
    ffmpeg's default resampler on the same signals: -100 to -105 dB. Level, pitch and timing are exact (within
    0.05 dB and 0.001 rad), and whole-number ratios (96 -> 48 kHz, 2x and 0.5x at 48 kHz) are clean.
    The -70 dB bar is the reviewer's choice: a 44.1 kHz music file (the common case) in a 48 kHz sequence gets
    distortion products at about -65 dB, audible on tones and quiet passages, masked in most mixes. It is the
    Lanczos-8 interpolator doing what it does (its images near the source rate fold back); the header's claim
    (Lanczos, eight lobes) is met. Medium-low severity.
F43 A 30 kHz tone in a 96 kHz file comes out at 18 kHz, -46.2 dB (should be removed: >= 60 dB down; ffmpeg -106).
F44 A 15 kHz tone at 200% speed (30 kHz) folds to 18 kHz at -46.2 dB. The stretched kernel used for faster-than-
    source reading attenuates too little.
F45 Two pieces of the same noise file joined (A src 2-12 s, B src 12 s on), a 4-second Constant Gain transition
    centred on the cut: the level dips 2.4 dB in its first and last second. clipSound() computes each clip's sound
    only 1 s (pad = sr) beyond its edges, so a centred transition longer than 2 s has silence where one side
    should still sound. 1 s and 3 s transitions stayed within 1 dB. Medium-low severity.
F46 See problem 3 (5.1 centre channel dropped).

LOUDNESS (25 checks, 0 failed)

COLOUR AND EFFECTS (79 checks, 3 failed)
F47 look33_resolve.cube (the same 33-point LUT as look33.cube with CRLF, tabs, comments and
    "LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE 0.0 1.0"): differs from the plain file by up to 242 levels. See problem 6.
F48 range_resolve.cube with "LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE -0.25 1.25": up to 189 levels from the specification's lookup
    over that range (same cause). Note: LUT_*_INPUT_RANGE is Resolve's keyword, not in Adobe's 1.0 text; ffmpeg's
    lut3d does not read it either. The plain 0..1 form (F47) is the ordinary one.
F49 See problem 7 (Video Limiter replaced by Hard Limiter).

AUDIO EFFECTS (24 checks, 0 failed)

EDL, FINAL CUT PRO XML, CAPTIONS (26 checks, 13 failed)
F50-F52 See problem 5. The lines Lantern wrote for one 48-frame clip:
    23.976: "001  AX       V     C        00:00:00:00 00:00:02:00 00:59:56:10 00:59:58:10"
    29.97 NDF: "... 00:59:56:12 00:59:58:00"; 59.94 NDF: "... 00:59:56:24 00:59:57:12".
F53 Hand-written 23.976 NDF EDL, events 001 a.mov rec 01:00:00:00-01:00:02:00 and 002 b.mov rec 01:00:02:00:
    Lantern puts them at frames 86 and 134; expected 0 and 48.
F54 Hand-written standard dissolve:
      002  AX  V  C        00:00:05:00 00:00:05:00 01:00:04:00 01:00:04:00
      002  AX  V  D    025 00:00:10:00 00:00:13:00 01:00:04:00 01:00:07:00
      * FROM CLIP NAME: a.mov
      * TO CLIP NAME: b.mov
    Lantern makes the incoming clip (at 4 s, from 10 s, 25-frame dissolve: all right) out of a.mov: it reads
    only FROM CLIP NAME and gives it to the last event. CMX 3600 names the outgoing clip FROM and the incoming TO.
F55 "001  AX  B  C ..." (B = picture and sound): Lantern places the picture only. readEdl() sets a "both" flag
    and never uses it. (Not every program writes B; Avid and older systems do.) Medium-low.
F56 Lantern's own EDL for a dissolve from interview.mp4 into broll.mov writes only "* FROM CLIP NAME:
    broll.mov" (the incoming clip under FROM, no TO). Another program reading it will take broll.mov as the
    outgoing clip.
F57 Hand-written FCP7 XML (as Premiere exports it) with a.mov <start>0</start><end>-1</end>, a Cross Dissolve
    transitionitem 100-125, b.mov <start>-1</start><end>200</end>: Lantern imports no clips at all (readFcpxml
    drops start < 0 and end <= start).
F58 Lantern's XML for a linked picture+sound: no <link> entries (the header says it writes them).
F59 Lantern's XML for media named 'Tom & Jerry <cut> "final".mov': <pathurl>file://localhost/Tom%20&%20Jerry...
    is not well-formed (raw &). Python: "not well-formed (invalid token)".
F60 ... and Lantern's own readFcpxml cannot read it back ("this XML has no sequence in it").
F61 A 200% clip written as Time Remap 200 comes back at 100% (the reader ignores <filter>).
F62 WebVTT "<v Roger>Fish &amp; chips</v>" comes in as "Fish &amp; chips"; "A &lt;b&gt;" stays escaped.
    The WebVTT spec defines these character references; YouTube's and most generated VTT files use them.

SCENES AND SYNC (7 checks, 1 failed)
F63 testsrc2 (3 s) cross-dissolving for 1 s into smptehdbars (xfade, ffmpeg): Lantern reports a hard cut at
    frame 74, near the end of the dissolve. The coarse 16-level histograms jump when large flat areas cross a bin
    edge together (score 0.48 against 0.05-0.24 around it). Premiere's Scene Edit Detection is for cuts; a
    false cut here would split the clip inside the dissolve. Medium-low; real footage dissolves less flatly.

MEDIA (12 checks, 5 failed)
F64-F66 See problem 1. Files: ffmpeg -f lavfi anoisesrc 48 kHz stereo 1 s, -c:a pcm_s24le / pcm_s32le /
    pcm_f32le into .mov ('in24'/'in32'/'fl32' + enda=1).
F67-F68 See problem 2. Files: the same noise as pcm_s16le / pcm_s24le in .mkv.


WHERE THE REFERENCE MAY BE THE ODD ONE OUT, OR THE BAR IS A JUDGEMENT
--------------------------------------------------------------------
- cut_copy.mp4 ("ffmpeg -ss 1.3 -c copy"): its edit list starts 1.3 ms before a frame boundary. ffmpeg moves the
  frames onto the boundary; ISO 14496-12 does not, and Lantern follows the standard. Allowed half a frame there.
- Edits in MP4 counted in a 1000-per-second movie timescale: Lantern's empty edits are quantised to 1 ms (a
  fragmented source rewritten is 0.33 ms off). Allowed 0.6 ms. Matroska keeps milliseconds, so AAC rewritten
  between MP4 and MKV is up to 32 samples off; allowed 1 ms (48 samples), as ffmpeg itself is further off.
- H.264+AAC MKV rewritten as MKV: ffmpeg's own rewrite moves the start by the AAC codec delay and says 2.047 s,
  the original 2.021 s, Lantern's 2.005 s; the duration check takes the original or ffmpeg's rewrite.
- Opus WebM rewritten as MP4 decodes 648 samples longer at the end, exactly as ffmpeg's own rewrite does (the
  DiscardPadding has no MP4 form in either); counted as right.
- The resampler bar (-70 dB) and the alias bar (60 dB) are the reviewer's, stated in the check names, with
  ffmpeg's numbers beside them.
- Kovesi's three box blurs: the module says "within a few levels"; the bar is 5 (sigma 30 was 3.5 levels off).
- Ultra Key's spill: measured as the component of each pixel's Rec. 709 colour difference along the key colour's;
  "taken down by a fifth" is the reviewer's bar (Lantern took off about 30% at Spill 50).
- Scene detection (F63): whether a dissolve should ever count as a cut is a judgement; Premiere's tool is for cuts.
- GIF exactness (F10-F11): no standard asks for it; good encoders give it.


VERIFIED RIGHT (all passing)
----------------------------
Readers, against ffprobe packet by packet (count, byte position, size, presentation time, keyframe flag) and
streams (size, rate, channels, display rotation):
- MP4/MOV/M4A: phone portrait 1080x1920 H.264 with 3 B-frames + AAC; 854x480 23.976 no B-frames + mono AAC
  44.1 kHz; 642x362 25 fps + 5.1 AAC; 29.97 with faststart; 50 and 59.94 fps; variable frame rate; a 90 kHz
  timescale; display rotation 90, 180 and 270 (Lantern's clockwise = minus ffprobe's); stream copy from the middle
  (edit list cutting media) and audio 0.5 s late (an empty edit); two audio tracks; audio-only M4A; fragmented
  MP4 with default-base-is-moof and with explicit base offsets; HEVC (hvc1); AV1; MP3 in MP4; a camera-style MOV
  with a timecode track; MOV PCM s16le/s16be/s24le/s24be/s32le/f32le/f32be and mono (frame counts right; see F64
  for the byte order);
- WebM/MKV: VP8+Vorbis, VP9+Opus portrait, AV1+Opus, H.264 with B-frames + AAC (29.97), H.264 + FLAC,
  H.264 + PCM 16/24, HEVC with two audio tracks and a subtitle track, a "live" file, tiny clusters; the last Opus
  packet's DiscardPadding equal to ffprobe's skip_end;
- AVI: MJPEG + PCM 16 stereo 44.1, MJPEG + unsigned 8-bit mono 8 kHz, MJPEG 29.97 without sound; packet data
  of H.264+MP3 AVI (times/keys not claimed there);
- WAV: u8, s16, s24, s32, f32, f64, 5.1 24-bit extensible, 96 kHz extensible, a LIST chunk of odd length before
  the data, RF64, odd-length data: every sample as ffmpeg decodes it.
Writers: remuxed through Lantern, decoded by ffmpeg with no error or warning, every picture identical (framemd5)
and shown at the same time, a seek to 60% finding the right picture, sound sample-identical from time 0 and in
step: the MP4 cases above, frag -> plain MP4, MOV -> MP4, VP9+Opus WebM -> MP4, MKV -> MP4, MOV PCM s16 (LE, BE,
mono), M4A; WebM VP8/Vorbis, VP9/Opus, AV1/Opus, H.264 MKV with B-frames, MP4 -> MKV, FLAC MKV. AVI MJPEG at
25, 29.97 and 23.976 with 44.1/48 kHz sound and odd-length JPEGs: clean, frame rate right, sound exact, the same
length as the pictures, seekable. WAV 16/24/32-bit mono/stereo/6 ch at 44.1/48/96 kHz: values right (clipped
for integers). GIF at 30, 25, 29.97, 59.94, 12, 23.976 and 50 fps: frames within 4 levels, delays adding up to
the clip within 1/100 s, none under 2/100, ffmpeg decodes them, loops for ever.
Timecode: every frame of the first 20 minutes and every 9973rd to 30 hours for 29.97 DF, 59.94 DF, 29.97 NDF,
23.976, 25, 50, 24 and 59.94 NDF equal SMPTE 12M arithmetic, and each reads back to its frame; negatives;
bad input refused; measured rates named (29.98 -> 30000/1001 etc.).
Edits: Insert, Overwrite, Add Edit, Lift, Extract, Roll, Slip, Rate Stretch, moves: no overlaps, whole frames,
no source outside the media, linked clips together (once a split's shared link is allowed for), refused trims
change nothing. By hand: Roll limits both ways, Slip limits, Insert into a clip (in point continues), Rate
Stretch (speed 2/3, same source), Speed 50% with and without Ripple (stops at the next clip with a note),
Extract with sync lock, Overwrite into a clip, a plain head trim stopped by the clip before, a reversed clip's
tail, a move that inserts, Lift on targeted tracks.
Keyframes: linear, ease (3u^2 - 2u^3), hold, Auto Bezier through its keys with no kink, text values, set/remove;
Add Edit and head trims through linear keys keep every value.
Mixer: 0 dB, Volume +-6, Gain + Volume, track volume, master, keyframed volume in dB, Pan +-100, track pan,
mute/solo/disabled, stereo and Left-only clips, a clip placed to the sample at 1 s from 0.5 s in, reversed
sound sample-exact, Constant Power 1 s and 3 s and Constant Gain 1 s transitions level within 1 dB, a fade-in
from silence at -3 dB half-way, pitch and level of resampled and speed-changed tones.
Loudness: EBU Tech 3341 cases 1-5 within 0.02 LU; mono 44.1 kHz, 5.1 pink noise (also against BS.1770-4's own
48 kHz filter), bursts, a short loud sound in quiet, hot white noise within 0.1 LU of ebur128; momentary and
short-term within 0.2 LU; true peak within 0.2 dB of ebur128 and of the signal's own peak between samples
(quarter-rate sine 45 degrees off its crests, a click, 997 Hz); silence and sub-block sounds give no number.
Colour: 33-point 3D LUT and 1024-step 1D LUT within 1 level of ffmpeg's lut3d/lut1d; exponent-form numbers;
DOMAIN_MIN/MAX; identity; incomplete files refused; Look intensity 50%. Curves: through their points, monotone
between them, no overshoot (150 random sets). Lumetri exactly identity at defaults; Temperature, Tint, Exposure
(linear light), Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Saturation (luma kept), Vibrance, Faded Film,
Vignette, Sharpen, wheels' brightness, HSL Secondary all act in their documented direction. Gaussian blur
(sigma 0.7-12) within 1 level of SciPy; box blur, median (identical), unsharp mask and threshold, Sobel, Emboss
at two angles; Invert, Threshold, Gamma, Channel Mixer, Solarize, ProcAmp (luma kept), Equalize, Brightness &
Contrast, Tint, Crop, flips; Corner Pin homography (5 quads) and warp within 1 level; Ultra Key on green and blue
screens (backdrop out, person kept, spill reduced, colours kept); nine pixel blend modes with see-through layers
against the W3C formula; Dissolve share; masks (area, edges, invert, opacity, feather, expansion) and tracking.
Audio effects: 12 biquads equal to the RBJ cookbook at 200 frequencies; the filter equal to SciPy's lfilter;
Bass/Treble, Notch, compressor static curve and make-up, Hard Limiter never above its ceiling and transparent
below it, Noise Gate, Delay impulse response, Amplify, Reverb tail, Swap.
Exchange: Lantern's own EDL at 29.97 drop-frame with V1, V2, A1, A2 and a 200% clip reads back to the same
layout; FCP XML round trip at 23.976 (plain names) within half a frame; project save/load identical. Captions:
SRT with BOM and CRLF, without numbers, one-digit and 100-hour times with a full stop, overlapping cues out of
order with <font>/<b>; SRT and VTT written and read back within half a frame at 23.976.
Scenes and sync: five hard cuts between six ffmpeg sources at crf 30 found exactly; none in a continuous zoom or
a fade through black; Synchronize finds +2.5, -1.37 and +0.456 s offsets within 10 ms with another "microphone".


NOT TESTED HERE, OR SEEN ONLY BY READING THE CODE
------------------------------------------------
- Nothing in a browser: WebCodecs decoding/encoding, the renderer, transitions (canvas), titles, the export
  pipeline's AudioEncoder timestamps (whether Chrome's AAC priming is cut), Chrome's own WebM seeking.
- VIDEO_TIMELINE applies Roll, Slide and Rate Stretch to the clicked clip only, not to its linked sound
  (Premiere moves linked edits together), so these drags will put sound out of step with picture. Read, not run.
- VIDEO_MP4_WRITE writes the sample rate as rate*65536 in 32 bits, which overflows above 65535 Hz (96 kHz PCM
  or AAC). Export uses the sequence rate (48 kHz by default), so it is not reached there. Read, not run.
- V.gifw.start(w, h, false) writes a NETSCAPE loop count of 1, which browsers play twice; export always loops.
- EDL source times are counted from 00:00:00:00 of each file, not the file's own start timecode (a camera's
  tmcd track); other programs relinking by timecode would miss. A convention question; not counted.
- The MKV reader does not read rotation (not claimed). AVCHD .MTS/.M2TS camera files are not a kind the tile
  reads (not claimed).


FOR THE RECORD (the media the checks make)
------------------------------------------
All inputs are built by run.py with ffmpeg's lavfi sources (testsrc2, testsrc, smptehdbars, mandelbrot,
rgbtestsrc, cellauto, sine, anoisesrc) and NumPy; see the make()/ff() calls in each section for the exact
command lines. The edit fuzz uses seed 20261126; the colour picture seed 7; the curves seed 3.
